title: Rise Up Like the Eagle
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The people said the road was long,
Their legs were worn and sore;
Isaiah said, "The Lord's not tired,
He made the farthest shore."

[Chorus]
But wait upon the Lord, my love,
And new strength you will find;
You'll rise up with the eagle's wings
And leave the dust behind.

[Verse 2]
Even the strong young men fall down,
The fastest runners too;
They stop and sit down in the dust,
And so, my love, do you.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
The walk home from the park is long,
And Beau's small legs just ache;
He breathes three slow breaths, holds Dad's hand,
And finds one more to take.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
So when your legs are all worn out
And you can't take one more,
Whisper, "Heavenly Father, please,"
He has new strength in store.

[Chorus]
mood: Walking music. A slow, even step under the voice, a tired boy's feet on the sidewalk home, each bar landing one more step and never hurrying. Fingerpicked nylon guitar keeps the walk, an upright bass marks the steps underneath, and each chorus lifts a little and hangs there, the way an eagle rides the warm air without flapping, before it settles back to the step. Steady and hopeful, a shade lighter by the last verse, never loud.
